previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with chronic abdominal pain, previously attributed to possible chronic pancreatitis or sphincter of Oddi dysfunction, was readmitted due to persistent epigastric pain, nausea, and vomiting. She had been discharged the day before to attend a gastroenterology follow-up, which resulted in readmission for further evaluation. An MRCP with secretin was performed, showing no evidence of chronic pancreatitis or sphincter of Oddi dysfunction, though decreased pancreatic fluid excretion was noted. Her pain was managed with oral hydromorphone and metoclopramide, and she gradually tolerated a soft diet. Presyncope in the ED was attributed to hypovolemia from poor intake. She remained hemodynamically stable, with no signs of acute bleeding or worsening anemia. She was discharged home with continued pain medication and plans for outpatient GI follow-up, as no procedural intervention was recommended at this time.
